## Motivation

The Ascend DeepSeek-V4-Flash tutorial currently lists EAGLE as the speculative decoding example and does not explain DSpark Compact deployment. Update the tutorial to document DSpark and provide a Compact configuration for Ascend A3 single-node PD mixed deployment.

## Modifications

- Introduce DSpark speculative decoding and confidence-guided Compact verification.
- Replace the EAGLE feature-table example with DSpark and update the model weights to `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8`.
- Update the single-node launch example for an Ascend A3 node with 16 NPU dies and TP/DP=16, using one shared script for Static and Compact modes.
- Add SPS cost-table profiling, Compact configuration, and scheduling verification instructions.
- Add accuracy, stability, and performance-comparison guidance while preserving the existing tutorial structure and reusing its verification and evaluation sections.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. This PR only updates documentation and does not modify inference code or model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. This PR does not change runtime behavior or introduce new benchmark results. It documents profiling and performance-comparison procedures.

## Checklist

- [x] Update the DeepSeek-V4-Flash tutorial.
- [x] Keep changes limited to documentation.
- [ ] Complete documentation formatting and link checks.

Profile the SPS table.** Stop the Static server with Ctrl+C first. Use a dedicated server: the profiler flushes +cache and aborts its profiling requests between measurement rounds. In terminal A, start the shared script with profiling settings: + +```bash +SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static \ +SGLANG_DSPARK_ENABLE_SPS_RECORD=1 \ +SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 \ +bash launch_dspark.sh +``` + +In terminal B, use the same SGLang checkout/runtime and a tokenizer directory accessible to that process: + +```bash +MODEL_PATH=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 +SPS_TABLE_PATH=/path/to/output/dspark_sps.json +python3 -m sglang.benchmark.dspark_sps_profiler all \ + --base-url http://127.0.0.1:6688 \ + --local-tokenizer-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \ + --batch-size 1 2 4 8 10 \ + --out "${SPS_TABLE_PATH}" \ + --no-plot +``` + +`--batch-size` is the request count per DP rank; with DP=16, the sweep sends 16, 32, 64, 128, and 160 requests. +Keep the sweep within the captured decode graph range and the running-request limit. +The profiler writes the SPS JSON and its measurement records, then reloads the table for a lookup self-check. +This static sweep provides an initial one-dimensional cost model; validate it on representative serving workloads. + +**2. Enable Compact.** Stop the profiling server with Ctrl+C, then restart the same script: + +```bash +unset SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN SGLANG_DSPARK_ENABLE_SPS_RECORD +SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact \ +SPS_TABLE_PATH=/path/to/output/dspark_sps.json \ +bash launch_dspark.sh +``` + +The startup log should report `DSpark ragged-verify scheduler enabled` with `mode=compact` and the SPS path. +Use [Functional verification](#functional-verification) to send requests.
